steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).

In a medium bowl, cream together the shortening and 1 1/2 cups sugar. Stir in the eggs. Sift together the flour, baking soda, cream of tartar, and salt; stir into the creamed mixture until well blended. In a small bowl, stir together the 2 tablespoons of sugar, and the cinnamon. Roll dough into walnut sized balls, then roll the balls in the cinnamon-sugar. Place them onto an unprepared cookie sheet, two inches apart.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes in the preheated oven. Edges should be slightly brown. Remove from sheets to cool on wire racks.

raw_recipe.headline: Snickerdoodles I
raw_recipe.description: This is a wonderful and easy cookie that my mother prepared for at least 50 years. Every time I take them somewhere everyone wants the recipe.

review.reviewBody: Bravo, Linda - this recipe produces the PERFECT snickerdoodle cookie (...and I KNOW a good snickerdoodle when I taste it!). For those who said it's not soft enough, there are 3 things I know of that can cause that: baking them too long, using butter instead of shortening, storing them improperly. Don't expect these to brown before you take them out of the oven - if they're brown, you overcooked them. And as odd as it may sound, butter-flavored Crisco actually works better than real butter in many cookie and pastry recipes. To store these, place them in an airtight container or ziploc bag with a slice of soft white bread; the bread will turn hard, but the cookies will stay soft. Just make sure you remove the hard bread and add a fresh slice each day (good luck - these cookies only last HOURS in my house!). Thanks again, Linda!

The first time I made them, they were rock hard. The second time, I really wanted a soft cookie, so I followed advice from other reviewers: 1) I used butter-flavored crisco; 2) I baked them ONLY 8 minutes, then left them on the baking sheet for another minute, then immediately transferred them to a cooling rack; 3) I put a piece of bread in the container with the cookies. They stayed soft for days!

Yum! My favorite recipe for Snickerdoodles. I like a little more flavor in my dough, so I add 1/2 teaspoon each of vanilla and cinnamon to the shortening, sugar, and eggs before stirring in the flour mixture. At Christmas, it's a family tradition to add red and green sugar crystals to the white sugar and cinnamon mix.

This was my first time baking snickerdoodle cookies and these turned out excellent! I made alternations based on other reviews. Butter-flavored shortening is a must. I added 1 1/2 tsp of Dominican vanilla extract. I planned to bake it for 6 mins so it didn’t overcook, but it wasn’t enough. The center looked uncooked. I realized this AFTER taking them out, and placing them on a cooling rack ( cooling rack is also a must) and eating one. So I put it back in the oven, same temp preheated and baked it for 2 more mins. It turned out perfect in texture. Slightly crispy on the edges, chewy on the inside. So the next batch will bake for 6 mins, cool, then bake for another 2 mins — I’m too scared to try it any other way, they were that good!

The 10-minute baking time is for real. They are very soft when they come out of the oven but they harden up. Also don't refrigerate the dough - make sure it is soft when you roll the balls. If they're too hard they pick up only cinnamon and no sugar.
Great flavor.

delicious! I used butter instead of shortening. I used 2 tsp baking powder as a substitute for the tartar (didn't use baking soda nor the tartar). I rolled the individual dough balls in a ziploc bag to coat with the cinnamon sugar. Baked for 8 minutes exactly and only one pan in the oven at a time

I have made this twice. I didn't have shortening either time. The first time I substituted 1/2 c. butter and 1/2 c. melted coconut oil. I also halved the cream of tartar. The cookies spread a lot and were extremely moist (doughy).... pretty addicting though with a slight coconut flavor. The second time I substituted 1/2 c. butter and 1/2 c. lard and put the full 2 tsp of cream of tartar. This time the cookies were quite tall and much fluffier. I didn't notice a lard-y flavor. I think time #2 was slightly better, but I loved them both and got enthusiastic feedback from others. Thanks!

This is my go-to Snickerdoodle recipe. It's simple, it's quick, and it's delicious. I use margarine in place of shortening, and I add 1/2 teaspoon of Cinnamon and 1/4 teaspoon of Nutmeg to the dough and a few shakes of nutmeg (and sometimes colored sugar) to the cinnamon topping, but those are my only changes. It's not only my favorite, but my daughter's, and several of her friends as well.

I added 1 tsp of vanilla extract, 1/2 tsp almond extract and 1tsp of ground cinnamon to the dough recipe to give them a bit of flavor and everyone loved them. Had a hard time having any left on the cooling racks to even put away!

One of my best friends used to make Snickerdoodles all the time. I found her recipe and it’s identical to this one! That made me happy! I made them exactly as this recipe said only I increased the baking time to 12 minutes. I tried 7-8 minutes and they weren’t done and were way too soft. I didn’t have butter flavored shortening so I added 1 teaspoon of butter flavoring. Other than than I made no changes. They are delicious! Soft and chewy and so yummy!

Good classic snickerdoodles. For my first (test) batch, I watched for the edges to look slighly brown. That never happened, so after 10 minutes of baking I took the cookies out of the oven. They were crunchy when they cooled. With the next batch, I took them out of the oven at 8 minutes. They didn't look browned, but they were just right. I stirred cinnamon chips into half of the cookies, and that turned out good, too.
Just made these, and they're damn good.

I have made this recipe for the last 10 years and it always earns complements. It is my husband's favorite. I use Penzey's cinnamon blend to get the nice, dark cinnamon look and it really takes the cookies' cinnamon taste up a notch. Every Christmas, I thank this person, her mom, and her family for sharing this wonderful recipe. OP, if you see this, I've been sending good blessings your way!
This is so close to my mom's Snixkerdoodle recipe! It's wonderful and I'll be keeping it forever.

I followed the recipe exactly. I baked each batch for 8 minutes, and then let them cool and deflate a bit before removing them from the pan. Every cookie was perfect! I used the bread in the container trick to keep them soft. I made a double batch for a party and every cookie was eaten.

I used butter (same amount) instead of shortening and it still turned out great. I also cut the recipe in half because I thought it was going to be too many and they were so popular with my family that I made more right after.
So good! A little crisp on the outside and light & airy inside. Yum! Definitely a keeper! (We used a GF flour for allergy purposes & they still turned out perfectly)

I’ve used this same recipe for 45 years. Needless to say, it makes the perfect snickerdoodle. I bake for 8 minutes and use the bread trick in my containers. They are the only snickerdoodle for my family!! My original recipe came from an old Menonite cookbook. Yummy.

I made these for our bowling league and everyone loved them! I did read some of the reviews and agree that when baking, only do it until set. Otherwise they get hard and don't retain their chewy center. Also, I haven't tried it with butter flavored shortening yet, but I plan on trying it next time after seeing all of the recommendations!
I add 1 t. Vanilla and a t. Cornstarch for extra chewiness. No one can eat just one!
